title: Patient debts the public hospital writes off
question: How much of what San Francisco General Hospital bills does it write off as bad debt each year, and is that growing?
finding: The City’s financial reports show $993.5 million of patient charges at San Francisco General Hospital written off as bad debt over the eleven years to June 2025: $79.1 million in fiscal 2015, a peak of $136.0 million in fiscal 2020, and $66.1 million in fiscal 2025. Set against what the hospital billed, the share fell: 2.7% of gross charges in 2015 and 1.3% in 2025. It is not rising. Charity care is counted apart: charges of $336.0 million were forgone under the charity policy in fiscal 2025. The report says “Patient accounts receivables are recorded net of estimated allowances, which include contractual allowances, allowances for bad debt, and administrative write-offs”.
how: From the note on San Francisco General Hospital in each Annual Comprehensive Financial Report, fiscal 2015 to 2025: the table of net patient service revenue (gross charges, less contractual allowances, less the bad-debt line, which the reports label a provision, a write-off or an allowance in different years) and the sentence on charity care. The reports print thousands of dollars. Shares are the bad-debt line divided by gross charges and by net patient revenue.
limits: Writing off a debt that cannot be collected is ordinary accounting. Gross charges are the hospital’s established rates before contractual allowances: net patient revenue was 23% of gross charges in fiscal 2025, so bad debt looks small against gross charges (1.3%) and larger against net revenue (5.7%). The label on the line changed over the years (provision, write-off, allowance) and the figures may not be measured identically. No patient is named or counted here. The same reports’ table for Laguna Honda Hospital prints no separate bad-debt line, and there is no such table for other debts owed to the City. Outside the hospital, 2 Board files since July 2014 speak of discharging a tax debt: an ordinance of 27 March 2020 handing the Controller the Board’s power to release the Tax Collector from collecting delinquent unsecured property tax, and a settlement of 24 July 2020, of a claim the taxpayer itself had filed, discharging $573,849 of such tax owed by Bundox Restaurant Corporation. 3 ordinances between 2022 and 2025 let the Tax Collector waive or cancel penalties under stated programmes; what was waived under them is in no file on disk. What would settle the rest: the Treasurer and Tax Collector’s record of debts referred for collection, collected and written off, by department.
